checks.detail: dtype float64, values in [0.000000, 1.100000]. Upstream's colourise helper calls np.angle on it, which is identically 0 for a non-negative real array, so the hue axis of that plot carries no information.
checks.name: the_phantom_is_a_real_float64_array_not_a_complex_one

checks.detail: the smallest strictly non-zero magnitude is 4.941e-324 -- a subnormal double -- and 52.0% of voxels are strictly non-zero at the default radius. Occupancy has to be measured above a threshold (here 1.100e-06), and denormal arithmetic can be far slower than normal arithmetic on some hardware.
checks.name: the_array_contains_subnormal_values_so_count_nonzero_is_misleading

checks.detail: above the 1.100e-06 threshold: filled=609734 voxels, hollow=130838 voxels (4.660x). The hollow variant is the shell only, so the flag genuinely changes the phantom.
checks.name: filled_occupies_more_volume_than_hollow

checks.detail: above the 1.100e-06 threshold, no voxel on any of the six faces of the (128, 128, 128) volume is occupied at the default radius=0.8, so the phantom can be zero-padded without cutting it. (With a naive count_nonzero the faces look occupied -- that is the subnormal noise above, not structure.)
checks.name: the_default_radius_gives_a_compact_interior_phantom

checks.detail: occupancy / boundary occupancy by radius: 0.8 -> 609734/0, 0.6 -> 1386662/16376, 0.4 -> 2093396/96354, 0.25 -> 2097152/98304 out of 2097152 voxels. `radius` is NOT an object radius in the obvious sense: reducing it from 0.8 to 0.25 fills the entire volume and clips against the boundary. The default 0.8 is the compact setting, and a smaller value is not a smaller object.
checks.name: decreasing_radius_makes_the_phantom_LARGER_not_smaller

checks.detail: two calls with identical arguments return bit-identical arrays, which is what makes this usable as a test fixture -- unlike filaments_3d (c14).
checks.name: the_generator_is_deterministic

checks.detail: the axis-1 projection peaks at 29.244797 and the z = 84 slice has 7367 occupied voxels, so both cells the example plots show real structure
checks.name: the_projection_and_the_z_84_slice_are_both_non_trivial
